analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md, adding lines 1370-1382 on Qwen inline MTP assistant behavior. The paragraph describes ordinary decode that may chain, target hidden rows appended to the assistant history, a prefill carry, a per-drafter opt-in (`supportsOrdinaryDecodeHistory`), and rollback env switches `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED` and `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY`. No code, config, endpoint, or deployment change is in the supplied evidence, so no control is weakened.

Relevant threat IDs: T-041 (prefix cache), T-028 (residual GPU data), TB-007 (inference engine). The documented hidden-state history and carry are request-owned in-process state. The text does not claim cross-request sharing, persistence, new disk artifacts, or new network surface. It states no policy top-two or extra readback. The adjacent unchanged text on SSD checkpoint coding already says speculative draft KV is never shared and only trusted prompt history is restored. Nothing here changes the T-041 posture (HMAC names, 30-minute TTL, salt scoping).

Remaining integration questions: the implementation file EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift and the new env switches are outside this doc-only batch and were not reviewed. Whether hidden-row history or carry is cleared on request retirement, cancellation, or slot reuse (T-028, TB-007) is not verifiable from this evidence. The configuration reference entries for the two new env vars are also not in the batch. The doc does not make false security claims. I identified no regression, but code-side behavior is unverified rather than shown safe.
